Engineering

Auxiliary Engine Start

The operation to start a ship’s auxiliary engine, which provides electrical power or essential services independently of the main propulsion engine, typically performed before arrival, departure, or critical shipboard operations.

Quick answer: The operation to start a ship’s auxiliary engine, which provides electrical power or essential services independently of the main propulsion engine, typically performed before arrival, departure, or critical shipboard operations.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Auxiliary Engine Start?

In this glossary, Auxiliary Engine Start refers to: The operation to start a ship’s auxiliary engine, which provides electrical power or essential services independently of the main propulsion engine, typically performed before arrival, departure, or critical shipboard operations.

How is Auxiliary Engine Start used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Engine room, prepare for auxiliary engine start. Confirm all safety checks are complete before initiating."

Why does Auxiliary Engine Start matter in maritime?

Auxiliary Engine Start matters because it supports clear communication in Engineering contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Auxiliary Engine Start?

Auxiliary Engine Start is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Auxiliary Engine Start belong to?

In this glossary, Auxiliary Engine Start is grouped under Engineering. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.
